newsitem.title: JAPAN: Poll shows support for Japan's Hashimoto slipping.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows support for Japan's Hashimoto slipping.

text.p: Support for the government of Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto slipped in the past five months to near 30 percent, according to a newspaper poll published on Wednesday.
The survey by the daily Mainichi Shimbun showed that support for Hashimoto's cabinet had dropped by seven points since April, when the last poll was conducted, to 31 percent.

The number of people who said they did not support the Hashimoto government increased two points to 23 percent, while 44 percent said they were not interested and two percent did not reply to the question.

Those who disapproved of the cabinet cited its failure to resolve a dispute over the heavy concentration of U.S. military bases in Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa and plans to raise the consumption tax to five percent from three percent next April as reasons for their lack of support.
The survey conducted over the weekend covered 4,236 people nationwide, of whom 66 percent responded.
Meanwhile, a separate poll by a major conservative newspaper, the Yomiuri Shimbun, showed support for Hashimoto was unchanged from a previous poll taken in July.
The poll, also published on Wednesday, showed a support rate of 49.6 percent, while the disapproval rate was 33.9 percent, a 0.7 point increase from the July survey.
The Yomiuri survey was conducted over the weekend and covered 3,000 people, of whom 69 percent responded.
